_comment: Shortening a long stretch of rest for practice, and the contract both
**Why a fixture rather than a shared function.** The app has to shorten
the score to play it and to count it (`lib/notation/longRests.ts`), and
the backend has to shorten it the same way before `build_timeline`, or
the analysis expects silence the musician was told to skip. Measured on a
perfectly played take: skipping a rest the timeline still contains takes
quality from 1.000 to 0.000 — `alignment_failed`, 'check you're on the
right piece' — and that is true for a two-bar rest as much as a twenty.
Different languages, no way to share code, so this file is the contract.
The rule: a run of consecutive bars that hold nothing but rests, at least
`min_bars` long, becomes the first `kept_bars` of them. The first, so the
bar keeps its number and any metre change printed on it; and a bar rather
than nothing, so there is a downbeat to come in on and the metronome has

cases.name: a run at the threshold is shortened
a run under the threshold is left alone
a long run is shortened to the same one bar however long it was
a bar holding a note as well as rests is not silence
a run that opens the page is shortened too
a run that ends the page is shortened too
a bar with no notes at all is not a bar of rest
a page with nothing to skip comes back unchanged
